sentences.text: Leonerasaurus taquetrensis was a small dinosaur that mixed ancient and modern features.
This creature measured 2.40 meters long, stood 1 meter tall, and weighed roughly 70 kilograms.
The single known fossil includes parts of the skull, jaw, spine, hip, shoulder, and legs, but lacks a tail.
Its front teeth were spoon-shaped with a rounded outside and a hollowed inside, similar to early long-necked dinosaurs.
At least 15 teeth lined one side of the lower jaw, angled forward by about 60 degrees.
The unique mix of traits in this animal suggests that early relatives evolved similar features independently.
Diego Pol, Alberto Garrido, and Ignacio A. Cerda named the species in 2011.
Fossils of an incomplete young individual were found near Cañadón Las Leoneras in Chubut province, Argentina.
Scientists classify Leonerasaurus as a basal member of the sauropodomorph group.
Studies place it within Anchisauria, appearing as a close relative to sauropods and Melanorosaurus.
The remains come from the Las Leoneras Formation, which dates to the Early Jurassic.
Researchers interpret the rock layer as spanning from the Pliensbachian to Toarcian or late Sinemurian to Toarcian stages.
The animal lived approximately 190 million years ago during the Sinemurian stage in what is now South America.
It is debated whether Leonerasaurus lived in the Late Triassic, as the lower age limit of the Las Leoneras Formation is not well-defined.
It is suggested that the evolution of primitive sauropodomorphs involved significant convergent evolution among diverse lineages.
